questions.question: Define heat and explain what happens when a cup of hot tea is left on a table, using the term thermal equilibrium.
questions.expected_answer: Heat is energy that is transferred from a hotter object to a cooler object because of a temperature difference. Heat flows from the hot tea into the cooler cup, table and air, so the tea cools; the flow continues until the tea and its surroundings are at the same temperature (thermal equilibrium), and then it stops cooling. The flow is fastest when the temperature difference is greatest.

questions.question: Explain conduction in terms of particles and describe an investigation to compare how well rods of different materials conduct heat.
questions.expected_answer: In conduction, particles at the hot end gain energy and vibrate more; they bump into neighbouring particles and pass energy along the material, while the particles stay in place; in metals free electrons carry energy quickly. Investigation: fix drawing pins with wax at equal distances along rods of the same length and thickness made of different materials (e.g. copper, iron, glass, wood); heat one end of each equally; time how long the pins take to drop. Pins drop fastest along the best conductor (copper); keep variables like flame, length and thickness the same.

questions.question: Distinguish between conductors and insulators of heat with examples, and explain why a blanket keeps you warm.
questions.expected_answer: Conductors let heat move through them easily: metals such as copper, aluminium, iron. Insulators do not let heat move through easily: wood, plastic, wool, cork, polystyrene, still air. A blanket does not produce heat; its fibres trap pockets of still air, a poor conductor, which slows the flow of heat from the body to the cold surroundings, so the body's own heat is kept in.
